messages.subject: [internship request] May-August Stan analysis in a Developing Country
parts:
I'm interested in supporting international development or health research, using Stan in a developing country (broadly defined), this summer (May - end of August).

I have worked with Stan over this past semester and have a background in evaluation using frequentist statistics. I am most interested in opportunities where I will receive close mentorship.

I can provide the majority (or potentially all) of my own funding.

Please let me know if you're interested or know of a potential opportunity.


--

messages.author: 29ce8550baceaeb0
messages.subject: Re: [internship request] May-August Stan analysis in a Developing Country
parts:
Josh - 

Let's have a chat. My number is 347 453 9455. 

We (Lendable Inc) are building a platform that will make it as easy for a US bank to lend to a good company in Sub-Saharan Africa as it would be to lend to a US firm. We're a seed-stage startup with 8 employees based here in NYC and in Nairobi. Our risk engine is built in Stan and R, and we're always interested in doing more work on it. 

I guess the big thing that we could offer (since we can't offer brand recognition) is fluency in "analysis as software development". We are very principled in how we build our risk engine, using Test Driven Development, git workflow, and run the team on agile principles. We're also take Bayesian analysis seriously. If you'd be interested in a summer project either here or in Nairobi, then we should have a chat. 

I see you were at CEA? Rob Wiblin is a very close friend of mine, and I used to live with his brother Gerald.

Cheers, 
Jim
